title: chat: Enforce per-marketplace plugin auto-updates
body:
Fixes microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog#8462

## Summary

Enterprise-managed plugin marketplaces can now specify `autoUpdate` independently of the user-controlled `extensions.autoUpdate` setting.

This change:

- preserves `extraKnownMarketplaces.<name>.autoUpdate` through managed-settings normalization; entries without an override retain the legacy source string, while explicit overrides use a JSON-encoded string so the managed setting remains compatible with the inline Settings object renderer
- carries the managed override into `IMarketplaceReference` and resolves it by canonical marketplace ID, so equivalent GitHub shorthand and URL forms share one policy
- replaces the global `hasUpdatesAvailable` boolean with the canonical IDs of marketplaces that actually have updates
- schedules checks when global auto-update is enabled or any managed marketplace explicitly enables it
- queues marketplace IDs reported during an in-flight update and acknowledges only IDs already processed
- targets automatic refreshes and updates to eligible marketplace IDs
- enforces `strictKnownMarketplaces` in both bulk and direct/manual plugin update paths
- preserves unrelated cached marketplace metadata during targeted refreshes
- regenerates the checked-in policy catalog with the updated managed-setting description

## Precedence

For each marketplace:

1. An explicit managed `autoUpdate: true` or `false` wins.
2. If `autoUpdate` is undefined, the marketplace inherits `extensions.autoUpdate`.
3. `strictKnownMarketplaces` is enforced before every refresh and update entry point.

## Tests

Added coverage for managed-setting normalization, explicit true/false values, undefined inheritance, canonical-ID matching, duplicate user/managed entries, mixed targeted marketplaces, global auto-update disabled, updates arriving concurrently, direct and bulk strict-policy blocking, and malformed policy entries.

Validated with:

- `npm run compile-client`
- `npm run valid-layers-check`
- `npm run precommit`
- targeted ESLint
- 169 targeted unit tests across managed settings and plugin marketplace/update services
- 229 build tests including policy conversion
- clean fixture-based policy catalog export

title: chat: enforce managed customization lockdown
body:
Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode-internalbacklog/issues/8464

## Summary

Adds VS Code-native enforcement for exactly three boolean managed-settings controls:

- `strictPluginOnlyCustomization`
- `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`
- `allowManagedHooksOnly`

`allowedMcpServers` and `deniedMcpServers` are pre-existing managed-settings data. This change does not add them as controls; `allowManagedMcpServersOnly` only changes which existing allowlist layer is authoritative.

## Code changes

- Registers the three boolean managed-settings keys in the existing policy pipeline and adds hidden policy-backed configuration delivery slots.
- Blocks standalone user/workspace skills, agents, hooks, and MCP collections when `strictPluginOnlyCustomization` is true, while preserving eligible plugin contributions.
- Prevents blocked standalone hook files and custom-agent frontmatter hooks from reaching execution.
- Under `allowManagedHooksOnly`, accepts plugin hooks only when managed `enabledPlugins` explicitly force-enables that plugin.
- Under `allowManagedMcpServersOnly`, uses only the policy-provided existing MCP allowlist as the positive allow source, while continuing to compose deny entries restrictively.
- Uses explicit MCP collection provenance so extension collection IDs cannot spoof plugin origin.
- Regenerates the policy catalog and adds regression coverage for provenance, dynamic policy updates, and bypass paths.

This PR intentionally covers VS Code-native enforcement only; it does not forward these settings into Copilot CLI or SDK sessions.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- `npm run gulp compile-client`
- 201 targeted policy, prompt, plugin, hook, and MCP unit tests
- changed-file hygiene checks
- clean-profile policy export
